Compared against the same weekday, not an all-days average, because weekends here run roughly a third below weekdays. Anything inside 10% either way is ordinary week-to-week movement. Today is the red bar and is still counting.

This will not match the number in Google Analytics, and that is deliberate. Analytics reported 8,297 organic visits that day against the 3,173 here. Same Analytics property, narrower cut: US visitors on www.testing.com, counted as engaged visits. Engaged is the important part. Analytics does not filter crawlers, and they are most of our raw visits, but a crawler loads a page and leaves so it never counts as engaged. Using the raw number would show traffic lurching around when only bot volume moved. Analytics also revises the last day or two upward as it finishes processing, so this figure can rise slightly.

Monetization livelaunchAug 18 · 12:00 AM

Checkout opened on testing.com. First customer order came through at 1:03 AM from Google organic.

This is the starting line, so there is nothing before it to compare against.

Cart rate since launch

Carts per 1,000 organic visits, split by the section each change affected, with the whole site dashed for reference. Only changes measured on cart rate appear here. Checkout changes move a different number and are judged on their own cards above, and a change to a page people click through to rather than land on gets its own chart below. A section line is the only place a section-level change can show up: STD GEO is about a tenth of our visits, so a big move there barely dents the sitewide line. Carts are the measure rather than orders because orders run single digits a day and cannot separate signal from noise for weeks. 11 days of data so far.

Cart rate on /std-test-pricing/

Share of organic visits to /std-test-pricing/ that add something to the cart. Counted on the page people viewed, not the page they landed on, which is why this is a separate chart and not another line above. Almost nobody arrives on the pricing page from search, they click through to it, so its landing-page numbers run single digits a day while it fires more than half of every cart on the site. One visit counts once here however many tests it adds, so this is a share of people rather than a count of clicks. The two charts count different groups of people and their heights do not compare.

Changes are recorded by hand, big ones only, and each needs the right scope and metric. To add one, edit changes.json.

attribution_html:
Where orders come from

Google Analytics, today so far · treat as directional, not exact
Bot traffic has been removed from every number in this section. Datacenter crawlers from Google Cloud and AWS hit this site hard, loading a page for two seconds and leaving. On 2026-08-28 that was 270 of 510 US sessions. Visit counts below are engaged sessions, meaning a real person read the page. Google Analytics' own dashboard does not filter this, so its traffic numbers will look several times larger than these and its conversion rates several times worse.
Read this before quoting anything below. These figures come from Google Analytics and are much less reliable than the revenue above. Analytics data runs through 10:37 PM PT, about 1h 58m behind this page. Analytics is also not recording checkout correctly yet: it logged 0 payment steps today against 0 real paid orders, and our purchase event sends no order value, so Analytics reports $0 revenue no matter what sells. Use it to see which pages bring people in, never to count orders or money.
